prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1350; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found a rear-end collision between two vehicles. Driver 2 stated that the trailing vehicle, operated by Driver 1, failed to stop in time and struck the rear of the vehicle ahead. Driver 1 confirmed the impact and said the lead vehicle slowed abruptly. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear of the lead vehicle and the front of the trailing vehicle, and the other driver's account matches what the photographs show. Several witnesses described the collision in the same way. A passenger in the lead vehicle reported a knee injury, and that injury fits the kind and force of an impact of this nature. However, witnesses and I both observed that the passenger was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which conflicts with the passenger's account. It is unclear whether all of the damage to the lead vehicle resulted from this collision. No earlier damage to either vehicle is known to me. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the lead vehicle.
